subject: Understanding the influence of predictors with different dimensionality

messages.author: 93e2d4587d90a376
messages.subject: Understanding the influence of predictors with different dimensionality
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to understand the structure of my open N-mixture model, but I am not entirely sure how predictors with different dimensionality (spatial vs temporal) influence the model.

Model example:

N[s,y] ~ Poisson (lambda[s,y])

log(lambda[s,y]) <- beta0 + beta.A * A[s] + 
                                                 beta.B * B[y] + 
                                                 beta.C * C[s,y]

Where index "s" represent predictors varying across sites and "y" across years.

How would you interpret the effect of each variable (A, B, and C) on abundance? Is the interpretation of the slopes dependent on the dimensionality of the variable? For example, is A[s] explaining *only* the spatial component of the population estimation?

All the best,

Alejandro

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: Understanding the influence of predictors with different dimensionality
parts:
Dear Alejandro,

yes, exactly as you say. The index of your covariates describes also the dimension along which it can explain variation (Note this is in your case where you organized the data such that a dimension is either space or time. One can write the model for vectorized data and there obviously that space-time dimension information would be lost.).

Best regards --- Marc
